blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Account deletion keeps the member's e-mail, name, phone and postal address) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: "UPDATE users SET deleted_at = datetime('now'), password_hash = NULL WHERE id = ?",
findings.recommendation: The proposal promises that the button "erases the member's personal data" (GDPR Art. 17, Art. 5(1)(e)), but delete_account only soft-deletes: it sets deleted_at and clears password_hash, leaving users.email, display_name, phone and postal_address (app/schema.sql:3-6) in the table forever. Scenario: a member clicks "Delete my account"; their row still holds 'ada@example.org', 'Ada', their phone and address, readable by anyone with database access and in every later export. Erase or overwrite those columns in the same UPDATE (email needs a unique placeholder such as 'deleted-<id>@invalid' because of its NOT NULL UNIQUE constraint, display_name a non-null placeholder, phone and postal_address NULL), so the orders kept for accounting point at a row with no personal data. Add a test asserting the columns are gone after delete_account: the current tests only check sign-in and sessions, which a soft delete passes.
findings.title: Account deletion keeps the member's e-mail, name, phone and postal address

findings.evidence:
def delete_account(user_id: int) -> None:
    """Deletes the member's account; their orders are kept for accounting."""
findings.recommendation: Nothing in the change or its proposal says how long database backups keep the deleted member's data, nor whether the analytics events keyed by analytics_id (app/account.py:11-13) are purged or detached when the account is deleted. The backup policy and the analytics store are not visible in the repository, so this is a question for the team (GDPR Art. 17, Art. 5(1)(e)): state the backup retention period after which the erased data disappears, and either purge the member's analytics events on deletion or confirm they hold nothing that re-identifies the member.
findings.title: Erasure of backups and analytics copies is not defined

findings.recommendation: analytics_id is not called by delete_account nor by anything else in the change, and the proposal does not mention analytics, so its purpose is not stated (GDPR Art. 5(1)(b)-(c)). Being a deterministic salted hash of the user id, it stays linkable to the member as long as the salt exists: it is pseudonymous data, not anonymous, and remains personal data after the account is deleted. Either drop it from this change or state its purpose in the proposal and cover it in the erasure (see R-privacy-2).
findings.title: analytics_id is added with no use in the change and is only pseudonymous
